newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania sees lower production in Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Scania sees lower production in Q1 '97.

text.p: Swedish truck maker Scania on Monday said its production rate in Europe would be about 15 percent lower in the first quarter of 1997 from a year ago in order to balance delivery delays.
The company also said in a statement that delayed deliveries could hit sales and earnings in the fourth quarter of this year.

"The French truckers' strike in the end of November has sharply affected French and international transportation firms because of transit traffic. In the short term uncertainty about demand for trucks has increased in France," it said.
It said deliveries of about 350 trucks produced in November at Scania's plant in Algers, France, to sales organisations in France, Spain and Italy have been delayed into December.
"The delayed deliveries may affect sales and the result in the fourth quarter," Scania said.
For that reason Scania said it planned to decrease the rate of its truck production in the first quarter of 1997 "in order to balance the delayed deliveries and the more uncertain market situation".
"Compared with the first quarter of 1996 planned European production will be about 15 percent lower," it said.
